issues.legal_issue: The special procedure for specified landlord-need eviction proceedings displaces an inconsistent requirement to obtain prior permission from a slum-area authority.
material_facts: The landlord obtained an eviction order on the ground of bona fide requirement under the special rent-control procedure.
The appeal raised whether the landlord had to obtain prior permission from the competent authority under the slum-area law before instituting eviction proceedings.
issues.conclusion: For proceedings covered by the special rent-control provisions, the slum-area law does not apply to the extent of inconsistency, and prior permission from the competent authority is not required.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14(1)(e), 14A, 25A, 25B and 25C of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, are special provisions; their non-obstante clause gives priority to the special procedure over inconsistent existing law. Chapter III-A therefore renders the Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1956, inapplicable to the extent of inconsistency, and section 19(1)(a) permission is not a prerequisite to proceedings under sections 14(1)(e) or 14A. The Court relied on Ravi Dutt Sharma v. Ratan Lal Bhargava, [1984] 2 SCR 614.

predicates.landlord_seeks_eviction_under_special_pr: The landlord seeks eviction through the special procedure for specified landlord-need grounds.
predicates.special_procedure_has_priority_over_othe: The procedure governing the eviction claim expressly gives its procedure priority over other laws.
predicates.other_law_requires_prior_slum_authority_: Another applicable law requires the landlord to obtain permission from a slum-area authority before bringing the eviction proceeding.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction through a special procedure that gives itself priority over other laws, and another law requires prior permission from a slum-area authority, the rule says that permission is not required.

issues.legal_issue: The two special landlord-need grounds for eviction are governed by the same principle of law despite applying in different situations.
material_facts: The eviction order under review rested on bona fide requirement under one of the special landlord-need grounds.
The Court considered that the two grounds concern eviction in different situations.
issues.conclusion: There is no difference in principle or law between the two special landlord-need grounds, although they apply to different situations.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that sections 14(1)(e) and 14A of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, do not differ in principle or law, notwithstanding that they address different eviction situations. It relied on Ravi Dutt Sharma v. Ratan Lal Bhargava, [1984] 2 SCR 614.

predicates.eviction_case_under_either_of_two_specia: The landlord seeks eviction under one of two special grounds that apply in different situations.

issues.definition: If an eviction case proceeds under either of the two special landlord-need grounds, the rule treats the same principle as governing both.
